evidence: Instances where plural/universal wording IS graded over the whole collection (good): (1) constraints gate hro_gate_shared requires 'exactly one card for that candidate in Applied' (gates/constraints/judge.toml:23). (2) hro_activity (functional/judge.toml:272) requires every successful board action on J1/J2 by any account, each card of every multi-card move, every undo, and the job filter to show 'all of that job's lines and only those' (both directions). (3) hro_candidate_private (:398) plus protocol K (functional/prompt.md:43) inspect 'every response' the candidate page receives, including socket/SSE payloads. (4) hro_candidate_view (:389) 'each candidate's own applications all appear'. (5) hro_bulk_move / hro_bulk_all_or_none / hro_bulk_places / hro_undo_restores check the whole set ('only some move' fails; 'none of the set moves'; 'any of the three enters'; Y, W, X all back). (6) hro_refusal_status, hro_observer_readonly, hro_candidate_no_staff, hro_anonymous and hro_thread_access enumerate every replay and say 'each ... refused'. (7) hro_activity_refusals 'none of the refused attempts'. (8) hro_thread_earlier 'until none remain'. 'Unchanged' guards vs legitimate side effects (good): hro_undo_conflict / B(12) lets the undo go ahead after a note on A2 and a re-order of a different card (rules:116 'Adding a note does not count'); hro_pol_failed_send accepts 'a local not-sent marker'; hro_stale_refused / hro_refused_put_back expect the refusing page to show the real place; hro_refusal_status grades only status so 'whether anything changed' is not double-deducted; functional/prompt.md:19 only forbids state changes by refused actions, matching rules:70,130. Cross-dimension perturbation of exact counts (hro_unread_counts 'rises by exactly two and his total by two', hro_restart 'unread counts ... unchanged', Lena's 1 unread) is refuted: tests/test.sh:207 runs rewardkit --max-concurrent-agent 1; the render gate opens no conversation (render/prompt.md:9); polish never uses Lena's conversation (polish/prompt.md:16). DEFECT - 'every card must satisfy all the rules' graded on one sampled offender: hireops_rules.md:106-109 says 'Every card must satisfy all the rules above ... If any card fails, none of them moves.' hro_bulk_all_or_none (functional/judge.toml:222-228) is exercised only by protocol B(6) (functional/prompt.md:35): 'Select V and Z and try Interview (Z would skip)'. After B(5) Applied reads Y,W,X,Z,A2 and Screen reads V, so the offending card Z is FIRST in board order (Applied precedes Screen) and LAST in selection order. The other refused set B(8) is a whole-set capacity count, not a per-card rule, and the mixed-stage success B(13) (A2 Applied->Screen, V Interview->Screen) has both cards legal. So 'every card' is never distinguished from 'the first card in board order' (or 'the last selected'). Also, the other per-card rules the same sentence covers are never applied to a multi-card set: the out-of-date-version rule (rules:94-97) is graded only on a single card (protocol C, hro_stale_refused), and hiring-manager per-card permissions (rules:87-89) only on single moves (hro_mgr_early_refused, hro_mgr_other_job). Secondary observation (Note-level, same pattern): in hro_undo_conflict both multi-card conflict cases touch the LAST card of the set (B(11): set V,X, Mei moves X; B(14): set Y,W, Mei re-orders W), so an undo validator that checks only the last card is not distinguished from one that checks every card (hro_undo_restores would still catch a store-only-last-card undo). Minor: rules:115 lists 'moved, re-ordered, rejected or reopened' as undo blockers; reopen is not separately probed, though reject-then-reopen is blocked transitively by the reject leg in a correct app. No run evidence: raw-evidence-index entries are scripted golden observations ('Not a configured judge run'); the defect concerns rubric discrimination, not golden solvability. Run verdict NOT EXERCISED.
counterexample: Broken app that passes: the multi-card move handler sorts selected ids into board order (needed to place them at the bottom in board order, rules:107-108), validates the stage step, version and role only for sorted[0], then moves the whole set. B(6) UI and replay: sorted[0]=Z, Applied->Interview skips, so the whole set is refused and nothing moves (hro_bulk_all_or_none passes). B(8): 3 into 2 places refused by a set-size count (hro_bulk_places passes). B(13): sorted[0]=A2 Applied->Screen legal, V legal too (hro_bulk_move passes). Yet selecting W (Screen) and V (Interview) and moving them to Applied moves V Interview->Applied, skipping Screen, and a multi-card move carrying a stale version for its second card silently overwrites a colleague's move - violating 'Every card must satisfy all the rules' with full credit on every bulk row.
suggested_fix: Add to protocol B and hro_bulk_all_or_none a second refused set whose offending card is LAST in board order and selected first (e.g. after B(10) select V in Interview then W in Screen and try Applied: V would skip; UI and replay; neither moves), optionally plus one multi-card replay with a stale version on its non-first card; no brief change needed.
